eligibility.rule: complete clean green laps only; pit, caution/mixed, restart, non-racing-state, off-track, close-traffic, and partial laps are excluded when the required channels exist

limitations: Load-zone names are provisional telemetry labels unless sourced knowledge supplies an official name.
Routine sampled onset/release and throttle timing are coarser than a native-rate event query.
Within-run phase changes can also reflect traffic, line, damage, weather, track state, fuel mass, and driver adaptation.
Tire wear remains a discrete pit-service observation; this artifact does not interpolate tread remaining within a run.
No session-derived tire-state change-point model is applied, so fresh/settled/worn phase labels remain unavailable.
CarDistAhead/CarDistBehind were unavailable, so traffic and dirty-air exposure could not be screened.
PlayerTrackSurface was unavailable, so off-track samples could not be screened.

brake_energy_proxy.definition: integral of brake fraction x vehicle speed through the zone

brake_onset_release.definition: 0.05 brake-fraction crossings; omitted when the transition is not observed

coaching.target_rule: no exact target without a valid aligned representative-lap comparison

steering_amount_work.definition: mean absolute angle, sign-change corrections, and integral of absolute angle x speed, on the recording's steering basis (lap_traces.steering: road-wheel angle when the setup states the steering ratio)

throttle_pickup_exit.definition: first 0.75 throttle sample after minimum speed plus zone-exit throttle

turn_in.definition: first steering demand crossing 0.05 rad of steering-wheel angle (0.05/12 rad of road-wheel angle) above the pre-zone signed steering baseline; absolute-angle fallback when no baseline exists; omitted and boundary-censored when the crossing predates the analysis window

phase_definition.confirmed_model: chronological early/middle/late thirds of this run's eligible laps with exact per-tire green-lap-on-set bounds after every tire has a confirmed zero-age boundary
phase_definition.fallback_model: chronological early/middle/late thirds with session-relative age bounds when at least one tire lacks a confirmed zero-age boundary
phase_definition.late_semantics: older-set/late-run proxy when green-lap age is confirmed; late-run proxy otherwise; never measured worn tread state
phase_definition.tire_state_labels: fresh/settled/worn remain unavailable until session- or history-derived pace/control/tire change points support inclusive green-lap-age boundaries

incident_points.note: Incident points are never treated as proof of physical damage.

limitations: No iRacing telemetry channel used here reports damage location or severity.
Pace loss, handling change, and incident points are never used to infer physical damage.
Pit-road, stall, service-active, and repair-countdown time overlap; stall time is not repair-exclusive time loss.
A positive repair timer is repair demand/availability, not proof that repair work was progressing; repair-active time uses intervals where the timer decreased.
A repair timer reaching zero does not certify that the car was fully undamaged.
Tow time confirms a tow/reset state but does not by itself prove physical damage.
Routine analysis is downsampled; use a bounded native-rate query for exact transition timing when needed.

limitations: Lateral offset is relative to the driver's session-median path, not an official centerline or measured track edge.
Positive offset means left of travel relative to that reference; it maps toward inside/outside only where signed-curvature quality gates pass.
Inside/outside and oval low/high fields describe observed movement direction, not absolute lane position or a recommended groove.
LapDistPct aligns samples around the lap but cannot establish a groove without recorded Lat/Lon position.
Tire odometers measure distance on the current tire set, not continuous wear; wear remains known only at a discrete service reading.
A detected migration is a repeatable path change, not proof that tire wear or setup caused it; traffic, cautions, line choice, and driver intent may contribute.

comparison_coverage.selection_policy: At most 24 comparisons: retain the latest usable window and the latest fully screened usable window with their runs' early-run windows, the first and last four candidates, then usable comparisons by largest absolute median pace change before unusable ones. All recorded laps remain in the timeline.

limitations: Window medians are observed comparisons, not estimates of a single cause.
Clean windows use the existing recorded eligibility screen; observed finish windows retain excluded laps and their reasons.

A comparison whose selected laps are all excluded, whose window spans a caution, or whose earlier and later laps a caution separates carries no pace delta or explanations and states why. Cross-run windows are matched by green exposure across a stop.
Cross-run exposure uses sampled green-time fractions from complete laps, not measured tire wear or exact physical green distance.

A saved test needs one run long enough to reach its exposure window; a test day is assumed to give runs of up to 20 laps. A run whose late laps need a longer run adds a first-20-green-lap window of its own clean laps, which offers a test only when it passes the same screens.
Corner timing uses recorded distance-binned samples; absent boundaries, gaps or fewer than two observations withhold that metric. Local traffic is not controlled.
Complete SDK-scored green laps crossing the checkered transition stay in observed pace windows; their clean-screen exclusions remain visible.
Steering is steering-wheel angle, not road-wheel steering: The garage setup does not state a steering ratio.

runs.valid_green_lap_rule: complete green laps with less than 1.0 s on pit road, at least 98% racing-state exposure when SessionState exists, excluding the first green lap immediately after a caution, off-track laps, and laps with close traffic for at least 10% of observed time

vehicle_dynamics.proxy_note: Wheel-speed divergence is a conservative tire-load proxy; corner-radius differences, banking, bumps, and sensor behavior can contribute.

limits: Dynamic platform, shock, pressure, and temperature traces are observational correlations; telemetry cannot uniquely identify which setup parameter caused a change.
Attribute setup effects only after controlled A/B runs with one change at a time and matched fuel, tires, weather, track state, line, and driver inputs.
Observed ride-height minima are not universal setup targets; legal and effective clearances depend on the car, track, ruleset, and complete setup.
Pressure and temperature traces do not establish tire wear; wear remains a discrete pit-service observation under the tire-wear rule.
